overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what phenomenology contributes to and challenges in consciousness debates. You'll be asked about pre-reflective self-awareness, the minimal self, ownership and agency, phenomenological critiques of how theories describe experience, and the limits of phenomenology.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: You're watching a bird and not thinking about yourself at all. What does pre-reflective self-awareness claim about this experience?

options.html: That you have no awareness of your seeing until you reflect
options.text: That you have no awareness of your seeing until you reflect
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. On this account, the seeing is already given as yours, without reflection.

options.html: That your seeing is given as yours, without a second act
options.text: That your seeing is given as yours, without a second act
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Self-awareness is built into the experience itself.

options.html: That you're thinking about yourself without noticing it
options.text: That you're thinking about yourself without noticing it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No thought about yourself is involved.

options.html: That the bird is aware of you watching it
options.text: That the bird is aware of you watching it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The claim concerns your awareness of your own experience.

forms.stemHtml: On Gallagher's analysis, what happens in thought insertion?

options.html: The person loses both ownership and agency
options.text: The person loses both ownership and agency
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The thought is still experienced as in the person's own mind.

options.html: Ownership is kept, but the sense of agency is lost
options.text: Ownership is kept, but the sense of agency is lost
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The thought is in the person's own mind, but authored by someone else.

options.html: Agency is kept, but the sense of ownership is lost
options.text: Agency is kept, but the sense of ownership is lost
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It's the other way around.

options.html: The person's narrative self replaces the minimal self
options.text: The person's narrative self replaces the minimal self
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The symptom concerns the components of the minimal self.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are contributions phenomenology makes to consciousness science? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Detailed descriptions of structures such as temporal flow
options.text: Detailed descriptions of structures such as temporal flow

options.html: Disciplined methods for producing first-person reports
options.text: Disciplined methods for producing first-person reports
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Second-person interview methods are one example.

options.html: A critique of treating experience as a set of inner qualia
options.text: A critique of treating experience as a set of inner qualia
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Experience is directed at the world, not a collection of raw feels.

options.html: A neural mechanism that produces experience
options.text: A neural mechanism that produces experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Phenomenology describes experience; it doesn't propose mechanisms.

options.html: A proof that physicalism is false
options.text: A proof that physicalism is false
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Phenomenology alone doesn't settle metaphysical questions.

forms.stemHtml: What do phenomenologists object to in the "Cartesian theater" model?

options.html: That it places consciousness in the brain at all
options.text: That it places consciousness in the brain at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The objection is to the picture of a display and a viewer.

options.html: That it describes experience too precisely
options.text: That it describes experience too precisely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The objection concerns the model's structure, not its precision.

options.html: That it treats experience as a show for an inner viewer
options.text: That it treats experience as a show for an inner viewer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Phenomenologists treat experience as the subject's lived openness to the world.

options.html: That it gives no role to broadcast in the brain
options.text: That it gives no role to broadcast in the brain
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The objection isn't about broadcast.

forms.stemHtml: What is Gallagher's term for the self as the immediate subject of experience, constituted by the senses of ownership and agency, prior to any narrative extended in time? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Gallagher contrasts it with the narrative self.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Gallagher calls this the minimal self.

title: Phenomenology's Contribution
